chapter.title: Sub-audible mantra & masked-language processing
overview: Controlled speech-priming, cortical recording and EEG studies show how acoustic cues can reach word recognition and, under some conditions, meaning through masking. The strongest, most relevant studies lead this chapter. Supporting sources explain the mechanisms that make a psychological or physiological response to externally delivered language a testable possibility.

Sub-audible mantra here means an external spoken recording mixed beneath music, with words difficult or impossible to consciously distinguish. Silent mental mantra means actively repeating a phrase internally. The index identifies what each study contributes to the rationale for I AM and where the evidence leaves an open question.
